turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you holding up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A huge storm's forecast for Wednesday and I'm working out how to prepare.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just listen while I lay them all out, and I'll ask for your view at the end.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could buy a little generator in case the power goes, but they're expensive and noisy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or just stock up on torches, batteries, water and tinned food, and ride it out at home.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mum lives inland and says we can stay with her, though it's a two hour drive with the kids.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's it, that's the lot. Your take?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Check how strong the warnings are. If they're advising people to leave, go to your mum's early, before the roads get bad. If it's just a rough night, torches, water and food at home will see you through.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? My train commute is unbearable in the heat. Any tips?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring a big bottle of cold water. Freeze half of it the night before, it'll still be cold by the afternoon.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Wear loose clothes in light fabrics, and if you can, stand near the doors where there's a breeze at each stop.
